title: Adding Stones to Rise A Group Exhibition of Sacramento-Based Artists
location: Axis Gallery, 625 S St, Sacramento, 95811, United States
description:
Adding Stones to Rise
A Group Exhibition of Sacramento-Based Artists
Artist and Curator: Adero Willard 
May 1 – May 29, 2026
Second Saturday Reception: Saturday, May 9, 5–8 PM 
Adding Stones to Rise is a curated group exhibition bringing together Sacramento-based artists working across multiple media, including painting, printmaking, ceramics, sculpture, and new media. The title was developed in response to the work and writings of the artists in the exhibition and to the regional presence of rivers that move through and around Sacramento. Water becomes a point of connection—flowing, sustaining, eroding, nurturing, and reshaping. It can lift, carry, overwhelm, or renew. The flow of a river may also be understood simply as the movement of material through the earth. In this context, adding stones may suggest burden, accumulation, protection, labor, or foundation; rising may evoke resistance, healing, survival, visibility, or change. 
Artists were selected to create a diversity of voice, perspective, process, medium, and identity, speaking to the expansiveness of Blackness and representing a collective of varying experiences. Each point is distinct, yet inseparable from the whole—reflecting how identity, particularly Blackness, can be understood as fluid, relational, and non-monolithic. 
Adding Stones to Rise centers the work of Black women and nonbinary artists—new to the region, rooted here, or returning. Together, these artists offer a collective meditation on movement, care, resistance, and transformation. This exhibition is one moment in an ongoing story. It is not the first of its kind, and it will not be the last. 
Curatorial Note: As a curatorial framework, stones, water, and rivers function as metaphors for ideas brought together in this space and may not reflect the specific themes or content of each artist’s work. 
Participating Artists
Debra Pitman, Laurelin Gilmore, Amari More, Victoria Kinyanjui, Khalia Morris, Tasha Green, Delgreta Brown, Alex Lowe, Sabrina Clark, Tasha Nicole

title: DataLab Office Hours (in person)
location: Shields Library, 360
description:
DataLab offers free in person drop-in office hours during which UC Davis researchers can obtain data science help and advice on working with their data. During these short, just-in-time sessions we meet with faculty, students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff from all domains across the University. Depending on the nature of your question and our availability, it may be possible to schedule a longer follow-up consultation after your office hours visit.

Appointments are not required. Please complete the brief office hours intake form ahead of time to help us connect you with the right expert for your question.

Common office hours help topics include:

Open Source Programming (R, Python, Julia, etc.)Reproducible research computing and data scienceResponsible and ethical data scienceData gathering, organization, databases, and experimental designData analysis, statistics, and explorationData visualizationMachine learning and neural networksText mining and natural language processingGeospatial sciencesRemote and high performance computingComputational pedagogy… and more!Please note that drop-in office hours are not offered during University holidays, academic breaks and finals week. Summer schedule varies. DataLab may only be accessed during Shields Library's business hours. Click here for detailed directions to DataLab.

Note: We are unable to provide support for assigned coursework (homework assignments, class projects, etc.) during office hours. If you need such help please contact your instructor or TA for assistance. If you need help with technical problems such system administration and hardware issues, check out the the UC Davis ServiceHub and/or contact your departmental IT.

This workshop will give participants a solid foundation on which to build further learning. By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to import data into a spatialite database, write queries to answer questions about spatial data, understand the difference between attribute queries and geometry queries, view spatial tables and views in QGIS, and use terminology related to spatial databases to facilitate future learning.

 

Concepts Covered: Databases, SQL, Spatial Analysis, Data Management

 

Speakers: Alex Mandel, Michele Tobias, Naomi Kalman, Holden Tal

 

This workshop will be taught by a team of instructors who use spatial SQL in their work and research.

 

Prerequisites: No prior experience is required, but familiarity with spatial data formats (raster and vector) is recommended.

 

Software Required: QGIS: available for all major computer operating systems at qgis.org

 

Please RSVP.

title: AI Literacy & Logic Workshop
description:
A free 1-day intensive workshop for College of Letters & Science majors covering foundational principles and skills for using Artificial Intelligence (AI).

 

The landscape of the academic and professional world is shifting. Whether you are an aspiring historian, a budding chemist, or a future sociologist, AI is no longer a "tech" skill—it’s a foundational literacy.

 

Developed through a collaboration between the UC Davis College of Letters & Science and DataLab, this 1-day intensive workshop is designed to unveil Artificial Intelligence. We’ve stripped away the dense math and complex coding to give you a conceptual, high-level understanding of how artificial intelligence systems work, why they matter, and how to make them work for you.

 

Why Apply to Attend?

In a single day, you will move from being a passive AI user to a critical, strategic collaborator. This training is specifically curated for L&S students to ensure you graduate with the competitive edge needed for the rapidly evolving, AI-driven workplace. According to a LinkedIn survey report, only about a third (38%) of U.S. executives say they're currently helping their employees become AI-literate. Meanwhile, findings from a 2025 Businesswire study found that 79% of workers feel they must learn new skills and that AI literacy is the foundation for long-term competitiveness. Students who attend this all-day workshop and complete required pre- and post-workshop activities will gain foundational and applied skills in AI, and receive a certificate of completion.

 

No technical background? No problem. This workshop has no prerequisites. It is designed for thinkers, writers, and researchers across all liberal arts, social sciences and STEM disciplines.

 

The curriculum is divided into four deep-dive modules:

How AI Thinks
Understand the "brain" of the machine. We’ll explore the theories of language and cognition that allow Large Language Models (LLMs) to function, and provide a framework for evaluating their potential and limits.

How to Use AI Responsibly
AI isn't a magic wand—it’s a tool with a history and consequences. We discuss the environmental and societal impacts, how to ensure the veracity of AI results, and why reproducibility is the cornerstone of ethical tech.

How to Talk with AI
Master the art and science of prompt engineering. Learn what happens behind the scenes when you send a prompt. Develop sophisticated strategies to get the exact results you need.

How AI Talks with You
A look at the future of AI implementation. From simple chatbots to complex autonomous "Agents," learn how AI is being embedded into systems and how to evaluate its activity.

 

By the end of this one-day workshop, you will be able to:

Define "AI" and distinguish it from traditional statistics and data science.Identify whether a real-world problem is suitable for an AI solution.Develop advanced prompting strategies that produce reliable, useful results for your research and career needs.Critically interrogate your own engagement with AI and its impact on our society and environment.Practice and grow your confidence in using AI in the rapidly evolving, AI-driven workplace. 

Who Can Apply?

All UC Davis undergraduate students with majors in the College of Letters & Science are eligible to apply. Registration priority is given to  Seniors (4th years) and students graduating in Spring or Summer 2026.  Other students in the College of Letters & Science are encouraged to register and will be admitted as space permits. Accepted learners are expected to attend all modules on their date of instruction.

 

Apply Now to Participate

This intensive, one-day workshop is offered five times during Spring Quarter 2026. Students should apply for only one date. Space is limited so don't wait to apply!

Registering for a ticket means you are applying to attend. This does not guarantee your participation. Accepted students will receive a confirmation email with the workshop location.Time: 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM with a break for a provided box lunch. Students must plan to attend all modules, including the networking lunch.Location: In person only. The classroom location will be emailed to accepted students in advance of the workshop.Cost: This workshop is free for undergraduate students and supported by the UC Davis College of Letters & Science. 

Questions?

Reach out to Mark Foncannon at mjfoncannon@ucdavis.edu.

title: JOURNEY THROUGH THE REDWOODS
description:
Iama Embodied Community
Tucked away in the Oakland Hills, this hidden gem is home to mostly second- and third-generation coastal redwoods, descendants of
the ancient giants that once stood alongside the sacred California grizzly and soaring condors. Today, these trees stretch skyward, carrying that legacy forward.

This will be an easy to moderate 3-mile journey, with approximately 350 feet of cumulative elevation gain. Along the way, we’ll encounter a variety of wild berries, from strawberries and huckleberries to the soft, velvety touch of thimbleberries and more.

Michael will share practical knowledge on
how to locate water in the landscape, and reading subtle signs from birds, trees, and leaves.
You’ll also learn how to recognize when you’re nearing the ocean, guided by the presence of specific plant species.

Elizabeth will offer insights into crows and ravens, marveling at their deep sense of community, reverence, and the way they invite us to
see the world with curiosity and wonder.
We’ll finish the journey with a relaxed tea gathering. Hot water will be provided; please bring your favorite tea and a snack to share.

title: NAMI Connection Support Group for Young Adults

description:
NAMI Connection Support Group for Young Adults is a free, peer-led support group for anyone between the ages 18 and 26 who has experienced symptoms of a mental health condition. Mental health conditions include anxiety disorder, depression, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, schizophrenia, or any condition that affects a person’s ability to lead a fulfilling life. You do not need a formal diagnosis to attend this support group; any young person concerned with their mental health and seeking support may attend. NAMI Connection for Young Adults provides resources to help young people build a support network and access help. Participants will learn together how to establish and maintain wellness. 
You do not need a formal diagnosis to attend. Anyone who is seeking mental health support may attend. 
What You’ll Gain
By sharing your experiences in a safe and confidential setting, you will experience connection, receive information about resources, and learn coping strategies. The group encourages empathy, productive discussion and a sense of community. You’ll benefit from other’s experiences, discover your inner strength, and receive support by sharing your own experiences in a non-judgmental space. 
  
NAMI Connection Support Group for Young Adults meets on the first Wednesday of the month (in person) and on the third Wednesday of the month  (via Zoom) from 7pm-8pm.  
To register for in-person or virtual meetings, please visit: https://namiyolo.org/support-and-education/nami-yolo-county-support-groups/young-adult-connection-support-group/.

description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

title: DJUSD Board Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM.  Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website. 
  
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance. 
  
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.
